Intervention(s): One-on-one education sessions plus FOBT and brochure vs. standard education group with FOBT and brochure.
Results: FOBT completion higher in the intervention group 65.9 %, vs. standard education 51.3 % (p < 0.001). No difference in FOBT completion by race/ethnicity (p = 0.655)

Outcome Type: Screening-Completion of FOBT; or up-to-date screening with Sigmoidoscopy, Barium Enema, or Colonoscopy
Intervention(s): FOBT distribution and education at time of annual flu shot clinic visit with reminder phone calls at 3 and 6 weeks vs. flu shot alone with usual care.
Results: Intervention group FOBT completion increased from 54.5 % at baseline to 84.3 % at follow-up (p < 0.001) vs. 52.9 % to 57.3 % (p = 0.071) in the usual care group. 68.0 % of intervention group became up-to-date with screening vs. 20.7 % for usual care group (p < 0.001), OR = 11.3 (95 % CI 5.8, 22.0)

Outcome Type: Screening-Completion of FOBT; or self-reported/documented Sigmoidoscopy, Colonoscopy, or Barium Enema
Intervention(s): Participants assigned to 1 of 4 interventions: Usual care; Standard Intervention (SI) with letter, information booklet, and FOBT; Tailored Intervention (TI), or Tailored Intervention plus reminder phone call (TIP).
Results: CRC screening use intent-to-treat analyses: control group 33 %; SI group 46 % (OR = 1.68, 95 % CI 1.25, 2.53); TI group 44 % (OR = 1.58, 95 % CI 1.18, 2.12) TIP group 48 % (OR = 1.91, 95 % CI 1.42, 2.56). Screening did not differ across intervention groups (p > 0.1 for all).

Intervention(s): Professional interpreter services provided at 4 of 14 clinics serving limited-English-speaking patients vs. comparison group of randomly selected adults representing 10 % of the eligible population.
Results: FOBT completion intervention vs. comparison group OR = 0.66 (95 % CI 0.44, 0.99; p < 0.5) year one; OR = 0.86 (95 % CI 0.57, 1.28) year two. No change in FOBT completion year one vs. year two in intervention (p = 0.28) or comparison group (p = 0.35).

Intervention(s): Trilingual health educator plus culturally tailored video and print materials vs. usual care.
Results: FOBT completion greater in intervention group 69.5 % vs. usual care 27.6 %; Age adjusted OR = 5.91 (95 % CI = 3.25, 10.75)

Intervention(s): Multi-modal intervention consisting of checklists, chart reminders, and feedback of screening rates to clinic staff. Rates of completion of FOBT at baseline and follow-up were assessed in 150 charts randomly selected from each clinic.
Results: There was a 14 % absolute improvement in FOBT completion (OR 2.56, 95 % CI [1.65-4.01], p < 0.001) for the intervention clinics versus control clinics, as measured by chart audit at 1, 2, and 3 months post-intervention.
